_comment: Filters applied to every company. Edit this file to tune what you get alerted about — no code changes needed. Set 'enabled' to false to turn a filter off entirely.

location._include_unknown: Some sites give a location we can't classify ('2 Locations', 'Remote', or nothing at all). true = let those through rather than risk missing a real US role.

roles._include: A job's TITLE must match at least one of these (case-insensitive, matched as substrings). 'analyst' alone covers business analyst, data analyst, financial analyst, research analyst, and so on.
roles._exclude: Titles matching any of these are dropped even if they matched above. Use this to cut role families you don't want.

_search_keywords: Sent to the search box of platforms that have one (Workday, Oracle, Amazon), so we pull a few hundred candidate jobs instead of every posting the company has. Keep these broader than the title filter above — this is a coarse pre-filter, the title rules do the precise work.

job_description._comment: Second chance for jobs whose TITLE didn't match. A posting called 'Associate, Strategy & Operations' or 'Program Coordinator' can still be an analytics role once you read the description. Those jobs get their description fetched and scored against the terms below; anything scoring >= min_score is alerted separately. Titles hit by roles.exclude never get here — an exclusion is final.
job_description._max_fetches_per_run: Each description is one HTTP request, so this is the runtime cost of the whole feature. The budget is shared across companies so one big employer can't eat it. Every job is fetched at most ONCE EVER (see jd_checked.json), so the first few runs drain the existing backlog and after that it's only genuinely new postings — a handful per run.
job_description._min_score: Sum of the weights of every distinct term found. A term counts once no matter how often it appears, so a description that says 'data' forty times doesn't outrank one that actually matches on substance. 5 = roughly one core term plus one tool, or two core terms.
job_description._require_group: Name of a group that must contribute at least one hit. Without this a job scores 5 on 'excel + stakeholder + metrics' alone — true of half of all corporate jobs. Set to null to disable.

groups._comment: weight = how much one hit from this group is worth.

job_description._exclude: Found anywhere in the description, the job is dropped no matter how well it scored. For role families whose descriptions borrow analytics vocabulary but aren't the job you want.
